change.title: pr-40940-flat
change.description: Fix concurrent group access to prevent NullPointerException
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: The reader thread is never joined, so the assertion can run before its last request finishes
findings.body: The test sets `deletedAll` and then checks `caughtExceptions` right away. The reader thread started at line 139 is never joined. A `groups()` call that is still running when the last delete returns can fail after the assertion at line 157 has already passed. That request overlaps the final deletions, which makes it one of the likeliest to hit the race. The thread also keeps running past the end of the test method. Keep a reference to the `Thread` and call `join()` (with a timeout) after `deletedAll.set(true)` and before the assertion. Also, the test only fails when the race happens to occur, so it does not reliably reproduce the bug it guards against.

findings.title: The three paged `getSubGroupsStream` overloads still dereference a null delegate
findings.body: `getSubGroupsCount` now handles `modelSupplier.get()` returning null when the group was deleted concurrently. The three paged `getSubGroupsStream` overloads at lines 256, 262 and 268 call `modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...)` without that check, so the same concurrent delete still ends in an NPE there. These overloads back subgroup listing, for example `GroupResource` at services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupResource.java:191. Consider applying the same guard, returning `Stream.empty()`, so the fix covers the whole race and not just the count.

findings.title: Hierarchy population can still NPE if a parent group is deleted concurrently
findings.body: In the same request path, `session.groups().getGroupById(realm, currGroup.getParentId())` returns null if the parent was removed after the child was loaded. `parentModel` then goes into `groupEvaluator.canView(parentModel)`, `toRepresentation(..., parentModel, ...)` and `populateSubGroupCount(parentModel, ...)` with no null check. This is the concurrent read/delete scenario the PR targets, but one level up. A null check that drops the orphaned child would close it.

findings.title: Typo in `groupUuuids`, whitespace-only line 117, empty line in the catch block
findings.body: The variable `groupUuuids` has an extra `u`. Line 117 contains only whitespace, and the catch block at lines 145-146 starts with a stray empty line.

contracts.action: Cached GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount returns null instead of throwing an NPE when the delegate group no longer exists in the database
contracts.equivalent_path: The other delegate-backed methods in the same adapter (lines 256, 262, 268) call modelSupplier.get() with no null check. The cached-field getters use `cached` directly and never touch the database.
contracts.before_after: Before: getGroupModel() was called directly, and a null result from the delegate threw an NPE (500 in GET /groups). After: the lazily cached modelSupplier is used, and a null result gives a null count. The JPA delegate always returns a non-null count.
contracts.visible_effect: GET /admin/realms/{realm}/groups with subGroupsCount=true (the default) goes through GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount into GroupRepresentation.subGroupCount (Long, nullable). A group deleted mid-request now comes back with subGroupCount null instead of making the whole response fail with 500.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent null in the JSON for a group that was just deleted. Other paths (the paged subgroup streams, a parent deleted during hierarchy population) can still NPE.

contracts.action: Removed the unused private helper groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement
contracts.before_after: The private method had no callers left in the file, so removing it changes no behavior.

summary: The change stops the cached `GroupAdapter.getSubGroupsCount` from throwing an NPE when a group is deleted while it is being listed. It now returns null, which `GroupRepresentation.subGroupCount` accepts. Two things remain. First, the new concurrency test never joins its reader thread, so it can miss the failure it is meant to catch. Second, the same race still causes an NPE in the paged `getSubGroupsStream` overloads and when a parent group is deleted during hierarchy population.
